caption: The drawing is a detailed, monochromatic illustration executed primarily in pencil, showing several objects related to textile and dressmaking, arranged neatly on a light, uncolored background. At the left center is a front view of a child's dress with short sleeves, decorated with horizontal bands and floral embroidery on the bodice and sleeves; measurements such as a "sleeve 2 3/4" are noted. Above and to the right of the dress, there are two close-up rectangular sections illustrating embroidered yoke and hem details, also annotated with dimensions. At the lower left is a back or alternate view of a blouse or bodice, tied at the neckline, while the bottom right corner contains additional textile details: a lace or embroidered bonnet, a vertical strip of lace, and two botanical or floral motifs meant for embroidery, all carefully sketched with intricate patterns. The overall composition is methodical, providing close-up visual references for the specific embroidery and construction details. At the bottom right, there is a handwritten signature reading, “Ellie Josephine Sterling,” alongside the date “June 27, 1890.”
title: Embroidered Dress & Mull Cap
